title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents

paper.authors: Maharana, Lee, Tulyakov, Bansal, Barbieri, Fang
paper.repo_license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (LICENSE.txt covers code and data)
paper.repo_note: Scaffold cloned shmsw25/FActScore (a third-party metric used for event summarization), not the paper's repo; the paper's own repo snap-research/locomo was cloned for this card. Event-summarization evaluation code is marked 'Coming soon' in README.

dependence.note: gpt-4-turbo is one of the evaluated long-context models (Table 2, Table 4) and the best-performing system in the paper; the core finding (LLMs far below humans, adversarial collapse) is a statement about these models. Data generation used gpt-3.5-turbo and text-davinci-003 (dead) but is frozen in the released dataset, so it does not affect re-execution.

claim.statement: With the entire conversation in a 128K context, gpt-4-turbo is the best long-context model on LoCoMo question answering with overall F1 51.6 (single-hop 72.3, multi-hop 51.5, temporal 51.4, open-domain 38.5, adversarial 15.7) yet lags humans (87.9) by ~36 points, and its adversarial-question F1 collapses to 15.7 vs 34.8 for gpt-3.5-turbo with a 4K window (Table 2; Sec. 6.1 findings 1-3).
claim.metric: Answer-prediction F1 (token overlap after normalization + Porter stemming; multi-answer: mean over ground truths of max over predictions; task_eval/evaluation.py f1()), averaged per question category and overall over 1,986 questions
claim.original_source: Table 2 (QA), Table 4 (event summarization), Table 5 (question counts: single-hop 841, multi-hop 282, temporal 321, open-domain 96, adversarial 446 = 1,986); no per-question model outputs released

protocol.model: gpt-4-turbo (alias, scripts/evaluate_gpts.sh --model gpt-4-turbo). App. C.2: OpenAI API 'as of May 2024' -> the alias resolved to gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, the same model as the live arm; the paper does not print the dated id.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions via legacy openai.ChatCompletion (global_methods.run_chatgpt; needs openai<1.0 or a shim)
protocol.prompt_source: task_eval/gpt_utils.py: CONV_START_PROMPT + formatted conversation ('DATE: ... CONVERSATION: <speaker> said, "..." [and shared <blip_caption>]', sessions in chronological order) + QA_PROMPT_BATCH + numbered questions; category 2 (temporal) questions get the suffix 'Use DATE of CONVERSATION to answer with an approximate date.'; category 5 (adversarial) questions become a 2-way choice '(a) Not mentioned in the conversation (b) <answer>' with random order (unseeded random.random())

params.batch_size: 20 questions per call (evaluate_gpts.sh); context truncation keeps the most recent turns so that conv + questions < 128,000 - 50 x batch (never triggers for ~16.6K-token conversations)
params.seed: not set; single inference run reported (App. C.2)
params.output_parsing: JSON dict {question_index: short answer} parsed by process_ouput(); 3 retries on parse failure

protocol.samples_per_item: 1 in the paper; re-run: 3 repeated runs x 2 prompt paraphrases (paraphrase only QA_PROMPT_BATCH wording, keep the JSON output instruction)
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: task_eval/evaluate_qa.py -> evaluation.f1 per question; per-category aggregation with evaluation_stats.analyze_aggr_acc (category ids in data: 1 = multi-hop, 2 = temporal, 3 = open-domain, 4 = single-hop, 5 = adversarial, matching Table 5 counts); adversarial answers mapped through get_cat_5_answer before F1
protocol.execution_environment: Single Python 3.9/3.10 process; requirements.txt (openai legacy API, tiktoken, nltk stemmer, numpy); no tools, no docker, no GPU for the gpt-4-turbo arm (RAG arms need the DRAGON retriever, not part of this claim). One full pass = ~105 API calls of ~20K tokens each, ~30 min wall-clock with the 5 s sleep in the code.
protocol.representative_subset: 3 of the 10 conversations (fixed ids, chosen to cover the length range) = ~600 questions x 2 runs; cheap enough that the full 10-conversation protocol should be run instead.

artifacts.prompts_path: task_eval/gpt_utils.py (QA_PROMPT_BATCH, QA_PROMPT, QA_PROMPT_CAT_5, CONV_START_PROMPT); prompt_examples/ (generation-side prompts)
artifacts.data_path: data/locomo10.json (10 conversations, qa, event_summary, observation, session_summary); images not released (URLs + BLIP captions only)
artifacts.notes: Non-commercial license; redistribution with attribution is allowed for research. Released data are the 10 conversations used in the ACL version (the March-2024 arXiv v1 had 50). No original per-question predictions are released, so only aggregate comparison is possible.

blockers: Model id given only as the alias 'gpt-4-turbo' (May 2024 API -> 2024-04-09 snapshot inferred, not stated)
Unseeded random choice order for adversarial questions and JSON-parsing retries introduce run-to-run variance that is not controlled in the original
Legacy openai<1.0 client in code; must be shimmed or pinned
Human reference (87.9) is a fixed number from the paper, not re-collectable

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (alias used in the paper resolved to this snapshot in May 2024)

successors: claude (current dated snapshot; repo has claude_utils.py)
gemini (current dated snapshot; repo has gemini_utils.py)
llama (open weights, long-context instruct variant, weight hash pinned; hf_llm_utils.py)
qwen (open weights, long-context instruct variant, weight hash pinned)

budget.unit_basis: ~105 calls per full pass (1,986 questions / 20 per batch, per conversation); ~20K input tokens per call (avg conversation 16.6K tokens + formatting + prompts), ~500 output tokens (20 short answers as JSON)

full.definition: all 1,986 questions, 3 repeated runs (x2 paraphrases -> 6 passes)

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1, capability_limit. Primary number: overall F1 51.6 with bootstrap 95% CI over 1,986 questions (approx +/-2 pts). SURVIVED if the median re-run overall F1 is within 51.6 +/- 3 AND the gap to human (87.9) remains > 20 points AND adversarial remains the lowest category (< 30). PARTIAL if overall F1 moves by 3-10 points but the human gap and the adversarial-collapse ordering hold. DEAD if overall F1 >= 78 (gap to human < 10) or adversarial F1 >= single-hop-level (the 'long-context LLMs hallucinate on adversarial questions' claim no longer holds).
judgment.notes: Temperature 0 but unseeded (a)/(b) ordering for 446 adversarial items; report the adversarial category with its own CI. Category-5 scoring maps the chosen option back to text before F1, so check get_cat_5_answer behaviour on verbose outputs. Successor arms with >128K context should still use the same 128K truncation rule for comparability.

user_checks: Accept the inference that the alias 'gpt-4-turbo' (API as of May 2024) = gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, making the live arm the exact original snapshot? (Alternative: contact authors.)
Run the full 10-conversation protocol (~$23 per pass, ~$136 for 3 runs x 2 paraphrases) rather than the 3-conversation subset - recommended.
Should the re-run seed the adversarial option order (deviation from original code) or keep it unseeded and log the draws? Recommend seeding and logging.
Is the CC BY-NC 4.0 license compatible with archiving full request/response logs in the project's public artifact (they embed the dataset text)?
domain_notes: The benchmark is fully self-contained (dataset in repo, rule-based F1), so this is one of the cheapest agentic-flagged cards; the 'agentic' part of the paper is the data-generation pipeline, not the evaluated claim. The scored answer is extracted from a batched JSON response, so format-following failures count against the model exactly as in the original. F1 uses stemming and multi-answer max, so verbose successor models are penalized; consider reporting an LLM-judged accuracy only as a supplementary, non-judgment metric.
